title: 6.2 Introduction to Conics: Parabolas

icans: I can write the standard equation of a parabola.
I can find the vertex, focus, and directrix of a parabola.
I can use parabolas to solve real-life problems.

vocab: the intersection of a plane and a ________________ cone
the set of points ______________ from a fixed line (the directrix) and a fixed point (the focus)
the line through the focus ________________ to the directrix

blocks.p: Mark the focus about 1 inch above the bottom edge. Fold the edge onto the focus 20–30 times.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Standard form (vertex (h, k)): vertical axis (x − h)² = 4p(y − k); horizontal axis (y − k)² = _______________.
Direction: p > 0 opens up or right; p < 0 opens _______________.

blocks.stem: Write the standard equation of the parabola with vertex (0, 0) and focus (2, 0).

notes: Focus and directrix: the focus is |p| units from the vertex inside the curve; the directrix is |p| units the _______________ way.

blocks.stem: Find the vertex, focus, and directrix of y = −½x² − x + ½.
Write the standard equation with vertex (2, 1) and focus (2, 4).
A headlight reflector is a parabola 6 inches wide and 1 inch deep. How far from the vertex should the bulb (focus) go?
Sketch (y − 1)² = −8(x + 2). Give the vertex, focus, and directrix.
